Slice: Suspend Neighbor

Step 4 of 9 in Keep late returners in check · after Neighbors — neighbor flagged · before Neighbors — neighbor suspended · State Change

Intent

Let the shed manager suspend any active neighbor, so someone who keeps returning tools late stops borrowing until the shed manager reinstates them. Usually the neighbor has been flagged for late returns. The system flags; the shed manager decides.

Trigger & Actor

The shed manager issues Suspend Neighbor from the Neighbors screen, for any active neighbor, flagged or not. The usual case is a neighbor the system has flagged for late returns, whose flags and late returns the screen shows; it also covers a neighbor who closed their account while suspended and signed up again with a different email.

The system never suspends anyone: reaching the late-return threshold only flags a neighbor. (Version 1 drew this trigger from a separate Flagged Neighbors screen; v2 folds that screen into Neighbors.)

Command / Input

Command: Suspend Neighbor

A NeighborId is a UUID.

FieldTypeRequiredRules / Validation
neighborIdNeighborIdyesThe neighbor to suspend. Must be a registered account (INV-SUS-10) that isn't closed (INV-SUS-2).

There is no reason or note field: nothing is recorded about why. The flag and its late returns are usually the reason, and a suspension from the Neighbors screen needs none. The command carries no "from" status: a late copy of an older request counts as a new request.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Neighbors @Shed Manager

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Suspended → context Neighbors Read by: Neighbors (status suspended, the suspended date, the open flags cleared, Reinstate offered), My Account (status suspended), and Neighbors To Flag (a suspended neighbor is never flagged). Check Out Tool, Extend Loan, Place Hold, Change Email and Flag Neighbor read it to refuse a suspended neighbor.

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
neighborIdNeighborIdyesFrom the command.
suspendedAtInstantyesThe UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. Shown as the suspended date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

The event never changes. A later Neighbor Reinstated lifts the suspension; a later suspension records a new Neighbor Suspended.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Neighbor Suspended feeds Neighbors, My Account and Neighbors To Flag, each specified in its own doc and eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

Suspension's effects are rules of the slices that refuse a suspended neighbor, each with its own reason the neighbor can see: a suspended neighbor can't check out a tool, including one set aside for them (INV-CHK-7, Check Out Tool), extend a loan (INV-EXT-7, Extend Loan), place a new hold (INV-HOLD-9, Place Hold) or change their email (INV-CEM-3a, Change Email). They keep what they already have: their loans stay out and they can return them (INV-RET-7, Return Tool), and their holds keep their places and can be cancelled. A set-aside they can't collect expires at the end of its collect-by date, as any other (Expire Hold). While suspended they are never flagged (Flag Neighbor, INV-FLG-5). A suspension lasts until the shed manager reinstates the neighbor (Reinstate Neighbor); it never lifts by itself and is never permanent. The neighbor isn't emailed: they see the suspension on My Account and as the reason whenever something is refused. Neighbors and My Account own how a suspension is shown.

  • INV-SUS-1: Only the shed manager suspends a neighbor.
    • Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused not-shed-manager.
  • INV-SUS-2: Only an active neighbor can be suspended.
    • A neighbor whose account is closed can't be suspended, because closed is final.
    • Suspending a neighbor who is already suspended changes nothing (INV-SUS-9).
  • INV-SUS-9: Suspending a neighbor who is already suspended succeeds and records nothing.
    • So a double submit, or a retry after a lost response, never records a second suspension.
  • INV-SUS-10: The neighbor must be a registered account.
  • INV-SUS-11: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path: suspending a flagged neighbor (INV-SUS-1, INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: Ana (N1) is active and shown flagged on Neighbors after three late returns within 90 days. She has the ladder on loan and a hold waiting on the cordless drill.
    • When: the shed manager suspends N1 from Neighbors
    • Then: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N1, with the time it was recorded. Nothing else is recorded: her loan and her hold are untouched.
  • Suspending a neighbor who isn't flagged (INV-SUS-1, INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is active and not flagged
    • When: the shed manager suspends N2 from the Neighbors screen
    • Then: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N2.
  • Suspending again after reinstatement (INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: N1 was suspended and later reinstated, so she is active
    • When: the shed manager suspends N1
    • Then: a new Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N1.
  • Already suspended (INV-SUS-9)
    • Given: N1 is suspended
    • When: the shed manager suspends N1 again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • A late copy after reinstatement (INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: the shed manager suspended N1, and then reinstated her
    • When: a delayed copy of the earlier Suspend Neighbor request for N1 arrives
    • Then: it counts as a new request: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N1 again.
  • Closed account (INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: N3's account is closed
    • When: the shed manager tries to suspend N3
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • Closed while suspended (INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: N4 was suspended and then closed their account
    • When: the shed manager tries to suspend N4
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." Its status is closed, not suspended, so this isn't treated as a repeat. No event is recorded.
  • Someone other than the shed manager (INV-SUS-1)
    • Given: N1 is active
    • When: a caller signed in without the shed-manager role asks to suspend N1
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can suspend neighbors." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-SUS-10)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: the shed manager asks to suspend N9
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Not signed in (INV-SUS-11)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: a request for suspending a neighbor arrives
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the shed manager on the screen they acted from. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-SUS-11): a request with no sign-in is refused first.
  2. not-shed-manager (INV-SUS-1): who is asking is settled next, before any other rule.
  3. neighbor-not-found (INV-SUS-10).
  4. If the neighbor's status is already suspended, the request succeeds and records nothing (INV-SUS-9). Status is tested with closed first: an account closed while suspended has status closed, so it gets account-closed, not the repeat.
  5. account-closed (INV-SUS-2).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-SUS-11
not-shed-managerOnly the shed manager can suspend neighbors.INV-SUS-1
neighbor-not-foundThere is no such neighbor.INV-SUS-10
account-closedThis account is closed.INV-SUS-2

not-shed-manager, neighbor-not-found and account-closed mean the same conditions as in Add Tool, Register Neighbor and Check Out Tool. neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screens, which offer Suspend only on listed neighbors. A missing or malformed neighbor ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: suspension is a state, and the command carries no "from" status. A request whose effect has already happened (the neighbor is suspended) succeeds and records nothing. A late copy of an older request that arrives after a reinstatement suspends again.

Requests at the same moment: Suspend Neighbor is decided against the neighbor's events as already recorded, one at a time per neighbor. A reinstatement or closure landing at the same moment is decided in the same order: whichever is recorded first stands.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. Nothing is emailed.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the shed manager may suspend a neighbor (INV-SUS-1). Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused not-shed-manager.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Suspended links a neighbor to a suspension. It holds no name, email or reason.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (this slice): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Registered matches slices/register-neighbor.md. Reinstate Neighbor and Close Account are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Neighbors, My Account and Neighbors To Flag. Check Out Tool, Extend Loan, Place Hold, Change Email and Flag Neighbor refuse a suspended neighbor; Reinstate Neighbor lifts the suspension.

Open Questions

None.
